sentences.text: Pre-operative multi-sequence MRI: axial T1, contrast-enhanced T1 (T1ce), T2 and FLAIR, co-registered, skull-stripped and resampled to 1 mm isotropic (BraTS preparation).
No necrotic / non-enhancing core exceeds the volume threshold (confidence 0.51). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The whole-tumour mass is predominantly left-sided (confidence 0.84).
An enhancing tumour component is present (confidence 0.99).
Whole-tumour burden is assessed as medium (volume tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.65). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The enhancing fraction of the whole tumour is mid (ET/WT tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.71).
Acquisition quality (cjv, efc, snr, sharpness, inu, contrast, entropy) is mildly outside the training cohort range (mean |z| = 0.55); interpret borderline findings with corresponding caution.

T1 and T1ce show a hyperintense lesion with a heterogeneous appearance, while T2 and FLAIR show a hypointense lesion with a slightly hyperintense rim on T2 and a hyperintense rim on FLAIR, indicating a mixed signal intensity with a possible mass effect.
The lesion has a slightly irregular margin on T1 and T1ce, and a slightly irregular margin on T2 and FLAIR, indicating a possible resection cavity or midline shift.
DEFERRED TO RADIOLOGIST: case confidence 0.51 is below the calibrated gate threshold 0.55.
